rationale: Both passages speak of eunuchs given a place among God's people. Isaiah 56:4-5 promises "the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths" a memorial "in My house and within My walls" and "a name better than that of sons and daughters" (BSB); Matthew 19:12 names eunuchs who "live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven" (BSB). In the New Testament of this app's BSB, "eunuch" or "eunuchs" occurs only at Matthew 19:12 and in Acts 8:27-39 (script search). On Bible Hub's Matthew 19:12 commentary page, only the Pulpit Commentary names the link, writing "(comp. Isaiah 56:3, 4)" in its note on the celibate life. Matthew gives no formula and shares no wording with Isaiah beyond the word itself, and the two passages describe different people: Isaiah's eunuchs keep the covenant, Matthew's third group have chosen their state for the kingdom. That is why the type is motif rather than allusion, and the label plausible: one named commentator compares the texts, and nothing in Matthew points to Isaiah.
